# MongoDB query shape optimization: sort, pagination, operators and sharded targeting — concept pack

> The shape of a find or aggregate query decides whether the planner can use an index: index-backed sorts avoid the blocking SORT stage and its memory limit, keyset pagination replaces deep skip, $regex, $ne, $nin, $where and $expr constrain index bounds, $in and $or become point bounds or index unions, projection can make a query covered, count, distinct, $sample and cursor batchSize/maxTimeMS carry their own costs, and a sharded query is targeted only when the shard key is in the filter. Compiled from MongoDB manual and Atlas pages plus the run's verified claims.
